fact: The RainDance Community Association's design guidelines, updated March 27, 2019, require approval before artificial turf is installed, keep it out of front and street-facing side yards, cap it at 30% of the rear yard and require screening so it is not visible from the street or any common-area tract.
quote: Approval is required prior to the installation of artificial turf. No artificial turf is allowed in front or street facing side yards. Artificial turf may not exceed 30% of the rear yard and will require screening so as not to be visible from the street or any common area tracts.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Landscaping and Maintenance (updated March 27, 2019), p. 12
notes: PDF downloaded and read with pdftotext on 2026-09-26. The only public version; the orientation packet says current documents are behind the resident login or by email request. Not confirmed whether the ARC still applies the 30% figure after Colorado's 2023 backyard rule.

fact: RainDance's design guidelines list putting greens with play structures, swing sets and sport courts as play equipment that needs approval before installation, must sit in the back yard at least 6 feet from any property line, and may be asked for more landscape screening or setback.
quote: Approval is required prior to installation. This includes, but not limited to, fort-style play structures, swing sets, climbing equipment, sport courts, putting greens, etc. Equipment shall be in the back yard and must be a minimum of six (6) feet from any property line. … Additional landscape screening or setbacks may be required depending on location of play area and proximity to adjacent properties.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Play Equipment (updated March 27, 2019), pp. 13–14
notes: The Play Equipment entry and the Landscaping and Maintenance turf entry never refer to each other; the guidelines do not say whether a green counts toward the 30% turf cap.

fact: RainDance's design guidelines require unimproved areas at conveyance to be landscaped with at least 50% plant material such as irrigated turf, shrubs and trees, and every rear yard to have at least 1 non-street tree, 5 shrubs, 3 ornamental grasses and 5 perennials.
quote: All unimproved areas at the time of conveyance must be landscaped using at least 50% plant material (not including the house footprint, walkways and driveway areas), such as irrigated turf, shrubs, trees, or other planted material. … Rear Yards shall have a minimum 1 non-street tree, 5 shrubs, 3 ornamental grasses and 5 perennials.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Landscaping and Maintenance (updated March 27, 2019), p. 11

fact: RainDance's design guidelines want shrub beds edged with a roll-top steel edger or masonry, flower beds and garden boxes 5 feet from property lines, and every landscape area watered by a fully underground automatic system on the Water Valley raw-water tap.
quote: All shrub beds shall have either a roll top steel edger or a masonry edge. All landscape areas shall be irrigated with 100%, underground supplied automatic irrigation system connected to the Water Valley raw water tap. … Flower beds and garden boxes must be five (5) feet from any property lines.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Landscaping and Maintenance (updated March 27, 2019), p. 12

fact: RainDance's design guidelines give a new owner 3 months after the home closes to finish landscaping, and let the committee extend that for planting season to no later than 7 months after conveyance if asked in writing before the 3 months run out.
quote: Landscaping on which a home has been closed shall be completed within three (3) months after initial conveyance of the property to the owner, with consideration given to planting seasons. Should an extension be foreseen due to time of year, written notice must be made to the ARC prior to the three-month expiration, at which time, the ARC will issue a new time requirement to the owner, but in no case later than seven (7) months after conveyance.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Landscaping and Maintenance (updated March 27, 2019), p. 11

fact: RainDance's Architectural Review Committee has 45 days after telling an owner in writing that it has the plans to rule on a request, a request it has not ruled on by then is deemed denied, and approved work must start within 3 months and finish within 3 months of starting.
quote: If the Architectural Review Committee fails to review and approve in writing (which may be with conditions and/or requirements), or disapprove, a request for architectural approval within forty-five (45) days after such notice to Owner, such request is deemed denied by the Architectural Review Committee. All improvements approved by the Architectural Review Committee must be commenced within three (3) months from the date of approval. … all work approved by the Architectural Review shall be completed within three (3) months of commencement, or within such time as otherwise specified in the approval from the Architectural Review Committee.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Introduction: Procedures (updated March 27, 2019), p. 2

fact: RainDance's architectural review application carries a $25 fee per submission, requires a diagram with a plot plan for every landscaping submission, and warns that the committee's approval is not Town approval and that a building permit may be required.
quote: Submit with Architectural Review Fee of $25.00 per submission … A diagram, to include plot plan, is required for all landscaping submissions. … I also understand that the approval does not constitute approval of the local City/Town building departments and that a Building Permit may be required.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Exhibit A: Architectural Review Application (updated March 27, 2019), p. 18
notes: The form's request boxes include Front Landscaping, Rear Landscaping and Play Equipment. Its phone and fax numbers are left out of the quote on purpose.

fact: RainDance's design guidelines allow only gas fireplaces and fire pits, in the rear yard and at least 5 feet from any property line (10 feet from any fence if taller than 6 feet), and hold water features to 4 feet, recirculating and out of the front yard.
quote: Only gas fueled fireplace and fire pit features are permitted. … Exterior fireplaces and/or fire pits must be contained within the rear yard … A fireplace or fire pit shall be located a minimum of five (5) feet from any property line … A fireplace or fire pit taller than six (6) feet shall be located a minimum of ten (10) feet from any fence … Water features not allowed in the front area of the property. In all cases, water features may not exceed four feet in height, must use re-circulating systems and the design should minimize evaporative losses.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Fireplaces/Firepits and Waterfalls, Water Features (updated March 27, 2019), pp. 9–10 and 17

fact: RainDance's design guidelines require approval for patios, want hot tubs built into a deck or patio at ground level in back yards, keep walkway lights pointed down and no taller than 24 inches, and require an engineer's certificate for a retaining wall over 36 inches, built only of brick, dry-stack stone or finished concrete.
quote: Patios … Approval is required prior to installation. Materials compatible with the home in color and size such as pavers, flagstone, or concrete should be utilized. … The equipment must be designed as an integral part of a deck or patio area … The equipment will only be permitted in back yards at ground level. … Walkway lighting must be directed to the ground and shall not exceed 24” in height … Any retaining/landscape wall in excess of 36” in height is required to have a professional engineer’s certificate … Retaining walls must be either brick, dry stack stone material, or architecturally finished concrete. Wood (i.e. railroad ties, etc.), unfinished concrete, or CMU blocks are not permitted.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Patios, Hot Tub, Lights and Retaining Walls (updated March 27, 2019), pp. 11–14

fact: RainDance's design guidelines require 3-rail fencing on corner lots and lots facing a street, park, open space or farm lot, allow no gate from a lot onto open space, a street or common area, and bar changes to the district's perimeter and open-space fencing except welded wire mesh.
quote: 3-Rail Fencing is required for all corner lots and for lots facing a street, park, open space, farm lots. … No gates will be allowed in any fencing to provide access from lots to open space areas, streets, or common area. … Perimeter/Open Space fencing installed by the District developer may not be removed, changed, or modified except for the installation of 2” x 4” galvanized welded wire mesh (10 gauge).
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Fencing (updated March 27, 2019), pp. 8–9

fact: RainDance's design guidelines require every fence an owner installs, inside and out, to be stained with a Sherwin-Williams color named RainDance Red.
quote: Fence Stain Required –All fences, interior and exterior, installed by Owners shall be stained using Sherwin Williams: … RainDance Red
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Fencing (updated March 27, 2019), p. 9

fact: RainDance's design guidelines require bulk landscaping material such as gravel, rock and timbers to be installed or moved out of sight of the street within 7 days of delivery, and bar owners from changing historical water flows onto a neighboring property.
quote: Gravel, rock mulch, bark mulch, timbers, block, or other types of bulk landscaping material or construction material must be installed on the lot or moved to a location not visible from the street within 7 days of delivery. … Owners are not allowed to increase or decrease historical flows of water onto adjacent property.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Unsightly Conditions and Drainage (updated March 27, 2019), pp. 8 and 16

fact: RainDance's design guidelines say the committee's approval is no assurance that work meets government rules or that no permit or approval is needed from a government body.
quote: Approval by the Architectural Committee will not constitute assurance that existing Improvements or proposed Improvements comply with applicable governmental requirements and regulations, or that a permit or approvals are not also required from applicable governmental bodies.
source_label: RainDance Community Association, Inc., Guidelines and Use Standards for Architectural and Design Review, Introduction: Effect of Other Governmental Regulations (updated March 27, 2019), p. 3

fact: RainDance's owner orientation packet says residential fencing is meant to stay open and minimal to preserve long-range views, and that the metro district installs the fencing at open spaces and along collector roads.
quote: Residential Fencing at RainDance will be open and minimally implemented to preserve long-range views. Fencing will be applied when necessary for privacy, security, screening and safety. Fencing character at RainDance is natural wood and metal. Fencing is installed by the RainDance Metropolitan District at open spaces and along collector roadways; Fencing is optional at all other locations.
source_label: RainDance Community Owner Orientation Packet (updated March 27, 2019), Fencing

fact: RainDance's owner orientation packet says owners belong to both the RainDance Community Association and the metro district, that the association's Architectural Review Committee reviews every architectural request, and that the governing documents are reached by logging into the community website or by email request.
quote: As a homeowner in RainDance, you are a member of both the RainDance Community Association, Inc., and the RainDance Metropolitan District. … Documents may be accessed by logging into the community website or you may request any documents by emailing clientservices@advancehoa.com. … The Association through its Architectural Review Committee is responsible for conducting reviews of all architectural review requests. No improvements may be made upon any Lot without the approval of the Association.
source_label: RainDance Community Owner Orientation Packet (updated March 27, 2019), Homeowner Orientation Guide
notes: The association's portal (rdca.eunify.net) refused connections on 2026-09-26; no newer public version of the guidelines was found.

fact: Raindance Metropolitan District's homeowner portal lets residents submit architectural requests, view community information and pay operation fees.
quote: Through the homeowner portal you may view additional community information, submit architectural requests, make operation fees payments, and much more!
source_label: Raindance Metropolitan District, Homeowner Portal page

fact: The four Raindance metropolitan districts are quasi-municipal bodies organized to serve the RainDance development under a Service Plan approved by the Town of Windsor.
quote: The Raindance Metropolitan District Nos. 1-4 (the “Districts”) were organized with authority to provide certain services and facilities within and without their respective boundaries to serve the development commonly known as “RainDance.” The Districts are a quasi-municipal corporations and political subdivisions of the State of Colorado … The Districts derive power from Colorado statutes and from a Service Plan approved by the Town of Windsor.
source_label: Raindance Metropolitan District, About page

fact: Raindance Metropolitan District wants each home's non-potable meter pit and curb stop kept exposed and clear of landscaping, rock, mulch, decks and patios, may bill damage to them back to the owner, and turns the irrigation supply on in mid-April and off in mid-October, weather permitting.
quote: The Metro District typically activates the non-potable irrigation water supply in mid-April and turns it off in mid-October, weather permitting. … The non-potable irrigation water meter pit and curb stop should be exposed and uninhibited by landscaping, rock, mulch, bird baths, decks or patios, etc. Costs associated with damage to the meter pit or curb stop may be billed back to the property owner.
source_label: Raindance Metropolitan District, Non-Potable Irrigation Water page

fact: Raindance Metropolitan District's 2026 irrigation owner guide says each home's non-potable meter pit is in the back yard, holding the hand valve owners open and close each season and the port where they blow out the system.
quote: Meter pit is located in the back yard of each home. … The meter hand valve is a gold/copper knob located next to the meter. … The blow-out port is located within the meter pit. This is where owners should blow out their system at the end of the irrigation season.
source_label: Raindance Metropolitan District, Non-Potable Irrigation Water: Owner Guide (2026)
notes: The guide's file paths name the Poudre Tech Metro District-Water Valley project; it is posted on the RainDance district's site and linked from its irrigation page.

fact: The district's 2026 water rate fact sheet says RainDance's irrigation water is diverted from the Cache la Poudre River through the Eaton and Whitney Ditches, stored in one of seven district irrigation lakes, filtered through 300-micron filters and piped to the non-potable meter in each yard.
quote: Getting the water: We divert raw water from the Cache la Poudre River through the Eaton and Whitney Ditches. Storing it: The water is stored in one of the District’s seven irrigation lakes. … Filtering: Before it reaches your property, the water is filtered through 300-micron filters at our pump stations. Delivering it: The water is pumped through pressure zones and a connected pipeline system that carries it directly to the non-potable meter in your yard.
source_label: RainDance and Poudre Tech Metropolitan District, Water Rate Fact Sheet 2026
notes: The fact sheet is shared by the RainDance and Poudre Tech districts; its system totals (homes, golf courses) cover both and are left out here.

fact: RainDance's community website lists the G.O.A.T. Ranch golf practice area at RainDance National as 65,000 square feet, while the club's own practice page gives 61,500.
quote: 65,000 sq. ft. G.O.A.T. Ranch golf practice area (now open )
source_label: RainDance Colorado, New Homes at RainDance National page

fact: RainDance's community website names Festival and Sugar Hills as the two residential neighborhoods of RainDance National, built by American Legend Homes and Trumark Homes.
quote: Own the best of vacation-style living inside the two residential neighborhoods of RainDance National – Festival and Sugar Hills. … Home builders at RainDance National American Legend Homes at RainDance National … Trumark Homes at RainDance National
source_label: RainDance Colorado, New Homes at RainDance National page

fact: Acadia at RainDance is a neighborhood of Trumark homes on one-acre homesites with a neighborhood park, close to RainDance National.
quote: Welcome to Acadia at RainDance, where you’ll find stunning new homes from Trumark Homes on one-acre homesites, a neighborhood park, and within a stone’s throw of RainDance National Resort & Golf.
source_label: RainDance Colorado, Acadia at RainDance page

fact: Emerald Estates, a custom-homesite neighborhood inside RainDance, backs every homesite onto RainDance National, makes every lot a walkout and lets buyers bring their own builder.
quote: Every homesite at Emerald Estates backs to RainDance National Resort & Golf, giving each property a direct connection to the golf course setting. … Yes — all homesites at Emerald Estates are walkout lots. … Yes — you are welcome to bring your own builder to Emerald Estates.
source_label: Emerald Estates (The Water Valley Company), Frequently Asked Questions

fact: Emerald Estates homes are built under their own community design guidelines, which the neighborhood's broker supplies to buyers, builders and architects on request; they were not posted publicly on September 26, 2026.
quote: Homes built at Emerald Estates are subject to community design guidelines intended to maintain a high level of architectural quality while still giving homeowners and their builders significant freedom to create a custom residence. … can provide the current design guidelines and help buyers, builders and architects understand the review process.
source_label: Emerald Estates (The Water Valley Company), Frequently Asked Questions: Building Your Home
notes: The FAQ gates the guidelines behind the broker; nothing on the site says whether the RainDance Community Association's ARC also reviews these lots or whether its 30% turf cap applies there. The broker's name is left out of the quote.

fact: RainDance National's Funk Yard, a double-sided driving range between holes 11, 13 and 14, uses antique vehicles, weathered farm equipment and cottonwood stumps as targets, a nod to the land's farming history.
quote: Nestled between holes 11, 13, and 14, The Funk Yard is our uniquely styled double-sided driving range. … Aim at scattered antique vehicles, weathered farm equipment, and cottonwood stumps—each one a nod to the land’s agricultural history.
source_label: RainDance National, Practice Facility page

fact: The metro district's 2026 farm field and orchard map shows apple, cherry, pear and plum plantings along RainDance's streets, with cherries harvested in July and apples in September and October.
quote: 2026 RainDance Metro District Farm Field and Orchard Map … Apples Sept. - Oct. Harvest … Cherries July Harvest … Pears September Harvest … Pears & Plums
source_label: Raindance Metropolitan District, 2026 Farm Field and Orchard Map
